question: Compare how tests ended for different fuels in CFI-G normal flames. Which self-extinguished and which were flow-terminated?
scope: Compare recorded Self-extinction (SE) and Flow terminated (FT) outcomes across CFI-G normal-flame fuel mixtures, keeping Unreported outcomes separate. Comparisons pool the recorded test conditions and do not isolate fuel effects; failed ignition is not extinction.

plan.title: CFI-G normal: test endings by fuel

charts.caption: Chart 1 shows Test termination by Fuel mixture for 133 reported outcomes, with Self-extinction counts exceeding Flow terminated counts in every fuel group.

title.text: CFI-G normal: test endings by fuel

warnings: Fuel mass flow is not air speed. SE means self-extinction; FT means flow termination. Neither failed ignition nor a blank is evidence of sustained combustion. Burn duration depends on how the test ended. Tad is a calculated adiabatic temperature; peak burner temperature is not flame temperature.

Outcome shares are descriptive, not extinction probabilities under controlled conditions. Flow termination is an intervention, not evidence that a flame would never extinguish. Linear regression is not applied to categorical outcomes.

introduction: Every listed CFI-G normal-flame fuel mixture had both self-extinction (SE) and flow-terminated (FT) tests, with SE more frequent in every group. These comparisons pool recorded test conditions rather than isolate fuel effects; fuel-specific Unreported counts are not supplied.
conclusion: In Chart 1, the recorded SE/FT counts were 25/9 for 30% butane (n = 34), 21/5 for 30% ethane (n = 26), 25/2 for 30% propane (n = 27), 13/6 for 50% butane (n = 19), 9/5 for ethane (n = 14), and 9/4 for propane (n = 13). **No listed mixture was exclusively self-extinguishing or exclusively flow-terminated.** These counts pool oxygen, pressure, fuel-fraction, and other recorded test conditions, so differences cannot establish that fuel identity caused a particular ending or estimate extinction probabilities under controlled conditions. The summary flags 46 missing pairs but provides no fuel-level Unreported breakdown; missing outcomes must remain separate, and failed ignition is not extinction. **FT is an imposed interruption, not evidence that a flame would persist indefinitely**; these observations are censored with respect to natural extinction. As general physical reasoning, self-extinction can occur when combustion cannot sustain adequate heating or reactant delivery, whereas terminating fuel flow removes the continuing fuel supply. The supplied evidence does not establish the mechanism behind these SE events or the differences between mixtures. No slope or R² is given because Test termination is categorical and linear regression was not applied.
